refinement.detail: Searched, found none applicable: RP-02's model delta is zero, so there is no representation to refine. The search WAS run against the one place this ticket could have reached for the model, and it was refused on the record MF-029 already wrote. The obvious way to make an existentially quantified argument recoverable is to have the model STATE it -- a `lastInternalAction` marker, exactly the mechanism `params_from_action_marker` already reads. Rejected twice over: the state pair already implies the element for every `v' = v \cup {i}` / `v' = v \ {i}` conjunct, so the marker would add representation to carry information the corpus already holds; and max_state_space_bound is at 279.9% of cap on this model, where MF-019 measured that a single boolean variable breaches it. Recovery therefore stays generator-side, which is also what keeps it cheaply revertible -- reverting is deleting a mechanism from one module, and nothing in the spec moves. Two representation choices inside the mechanism were made the cheaper way and are recorded here rather than left implicit. (1) The recipe keeps EVERY matching set conjunct as a cross-checking witness instead of picking one, which costs a tuple per parameter and buys a real refusal: `Deliver(i)` is witnessed by both `queue` and `delivered`, and witnesses that disagree yield UNCHECKED rather than a silent winner. (2) `consumed_observations` was added as a SEPARATE property rather than folded into `unavailable_checks`, because the two claims are different strengths -- set-membership spends "which element moved in v", it does not make the whole after-value of v tautological the way `written-through` does, and collapsing them would have overstated the price of the recovery.

summary: RP-02: set-membership parameter recovery closes the ex4 oracle leak (EV-01-DF-01) and the audit now reports what the run measured (EV-02-DF-03). A fourth mechanism recovers the element that entered or left a set, cross-checked across every such conjunct of the action; ex4 goes 0 of 5 -> 5 of 5 parameters and all 330 cases carry a real argument where every one carried UNCHECKED. The adapter reads case.input.params and never touches case.after; an unrecovered argument is a hard failure there. Generation stays deterministic (two regenerations byte-identical). The audit is rendered from the corpus it audits: the sentence 'Every parameter of every action is recoverable from its state pair' is gone, nine tests assert it cannot return, an unmeasured audit declares itself STATIC, a class that recovered nothing is UNRECOVERABLE ON THIS CORPUS whatever the syntax promised, and marker-declared arguments are reported as model-declared rather than credited as recovered. THE HONEST NEGATIVE: the reconstructed 12-mutant catalog is identical before and after -- guard relaxation still 0 of 3 by corpus, 3 of 3 by hand-written tests -- because all 330 recovered arguments are arguments the guard ACCEPTS and 0 are rejected inputs (220 refusable pairs exist that a state graph can never emit). Removing the leakage half of EV-02's two causes moves nothing, so the whole remaining failure is the structural half. Separately, the wrong-item class seeded_faults.toml declined to seed as unmeasurable is killed on BOTH instruments; that caveat was a prediction never run and is amended in place. Zero TLA+ model delta.

assertions: Set-membership actions recover their argument; ex4's corpus carries real params, not UNCHECKED.

ticket.model_delta_result: ZERO, verified: `diff -r specs/tickets/RP-02/current specs/tickets/RP-02/desired` is empty, `git diff --stat HEAD -- specs/current specs/program_model` is empty, and TLC on ticket current is green with EV-02's exact numbers (32,122,220 generated / 1,292,951 distinct / depth 26, 0 left on queue). Nothing was added to the model: parameter recovery is generator-side by construction, and MF-029 already recorded why a `lastInternalAction` marker was rejected -- the state pair already implies the argument, and max_state_space_bound cannot afford another variable.
ticket.objective: MF-029 recovers 0 of 5 parameters on a set-membership model, so every generated case carries `params={'i': UNCHECKED}` (or `{}`) and the adapter is forced to re-derive the action argument by diffing before against after -- i.e. from the ORACLE. Two eval runs found this independently, one from inside and one from outside. It is why guard relaxation is unkillable in the measured catalog: the adapter only ever calls the action with the argument that was going to succeed. Meanwhile `param_recovery_audit.md` states "every parameter of every action is recoverable from its state pair" on a run reporting 0/38 cases carrying arguments -- the audit contradicts the corpus it audits, which is the honest-in-prose/misleading-in-artifact class this epic keeps finding. Fix the recovery for set-membership actions (the argument is the element that entered or left the set), and make the audit report what the run measured. If recovery genuinely cannot be done for a class, the audit must say UNRECOVERABLE for it -- never "recoverable" over a corpus that carries nothing.
ticket.result: A fourth recovery mechanism, `set-membership`, recovers the argument of an action whose body is `v' = v \cup {i}` or `v' = v \ {i}` -- the element that entered or left the set -- cross-checked across EVERY such conjunct of the action, so `Accept(i)` is witnessed by both `inbox` and `accepted` and a disagreement or a two-element move yields UNCHECKED rather than a guess. ex4 goes from 0 of 5 parameters to 5 of 5: all 330 cases carry `params={'i': 'i1'}` or `{'i': 'i2'}` where every one previously carried UNCHECKED. The ex4 adapter now reads `case.input.params` and never touches `case.after`; an unrecovered argument is a hard failure there rather than a silent no-op. Determinism survives: two independent regenerations are byte-identical, new `cases.py` sha256 944189052623960aea..., recorded in the fixture's corpus_fingerprint.txt beside EV-01's. The audit is now rendered FROM THE CORPUS IT AUDITS. The sentence "Every parameter of every action is recoverable from its state pair" is gone and nine tests assert it can never return; an unmeasured audit declares itself STATIC, an empty corpus makes no claim, a class that recovered nothing is UNRECOVERABLE ON THIS CORPUS whatever the syntax promised, and arguments a model states through its own action marker are reported as model-declared rather than credited as recovered (which is what made `reminder_worker` print the universal claim over seven nullary actions). THE HONEST NEGATIVE, measured on both instruments: the reconstructed 12-mutant catalog is identical before and after -- guard relaxation is still 0 of 3 killed by the corpus and 3 of 3 by the hand-written suite. Counted rather than asserted: all 330 recovered arguments are arguments the guard ACCEPTS, 0 are rejected inputs, and 220 refusable argument/before-state pairs exist in the state space that a state graph can never emit. EV-02 named two compounding causes; RP-02 removes the oracle-leakage half and the class does not move, so the whole of the remaining failure is attributable to the structural half. Separately, the wrong-item class that seeded_faults.toml declined to seed as unmeasurable turns out to be killed on BOTH instruments -- that caveat was a prediction never run, and it is amended in place without altering an answer-key row.
